sentences.zh: 王渾

translations.literal: Wang Hun (section heading).
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun

sentences.zh: 王渾，字玄沖，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Hun, courtesy name Xuanchong, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun, whose courtesy name was Xuanchong, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父昶，魏司空。

translations.literal: His father Chang was Wei Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Chang had served the Wei as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 渾沈雅有器量。

translations.literal: Hun was deep and refined and had vessel and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He was steady, refined, and broad-minded.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵京陵侯，辟大將軍曹爽掾。

translations.literal: He inherited his father’s noble rank Marquis of Jingling, was summoned as aide to Grand General Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to his father’s marquisate of Jingling and was hired as an aide on Grand General Cao Shuang’s staff.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，隨例免。

translations.literal: Shuang was executed; following precedent he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang fell he lost his post like the rest of the staff.

sentences.zh: 起為懷令，參文帝安東軍事，累遷散騎黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He rose as magistrate of Huai, participated in Emperor Wen’s Anton military affairs, promoted in stages to Cavalier Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as magistrate of Huai, joined Prince Wen’s eastern command staff, and rose through posts as cavalier gentleman at the Yellow Gate and regular cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 咸熙中為越騎校尉。

translations.literal: In Xianxi he was Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianxi he commanded the agile cavalry regiment.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，加揚烈將軍，遷徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he was added General Who Spreads Ferocity, promoted Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne he was named General Who Spreads Ferocity and inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 時年荒歲饑，渾開倉振贍，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: At the time years were barren and the age famished; Hun opened granaries and relieved and fed; the hundred surnames relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In a time of famine he opened the granaries for relief, and the people owed him their lives.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，增封邑千八百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, his fief was increased by one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi his fief gained another eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷東中郎將，監淮北諸軍事，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted General of the Eastern Center, overseer of all military affairs north of the Huai, garrisoned Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became eastern center general, supervised Huai-north operations, and was stationed at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 數陳損益，多見納用。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he presented harm and benefit; much was accepted and used.
translations.idiomatic: He often submitted policy advice, much of which the court adopted.

sentences.zh: 轉征虜將軍、監豫州諸軍事、假節，領豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred General Who Conquers Captives, overseer of Yu Province military affairs, credential staff, concurrent Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who conquers captives with acting credentials, overseer of Yu military affairs, and inspector of the province.

sentences.zh: 渾與吳接境，宣佈威信，前後降附甚多。

translations.literal: Hun bordered Wu, proclaimed trust and awe; before and after, those who surrendered and attached were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Wu frontier he projected authority and won a steady stream of defections.

sentences.zh: 吳將薛瑩、魯淑眾號十萬，淑向弋陽，瑩向新息。

translations.literal: Wu generals Xue Ying and Lu Shu, their hosts titled one hundred thousand—Shu toward Yiyang, Ying toward Xinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu generals Xue Ying and Lu Shu advanced with a force said to number one hundred thousand—Lu Shu toward Yiyang, Xue Ying toward Xinxi.

sentences.zh: 時州兵並放休息，眾裁一旅，浮淮潛濟，出其不意，瑩等不虞晉師之至。

translations.literal: At the time provincial troops were all released to rest; the host was only one brigade; they floated the Huai and secretly crossed, coming beyond expectation; Ying and the rest did not expect Jin troops’ arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial troops were on leave and he had only a single brigade, but he crossed the Huai by stealth and caught Ying off guard.

sentences.zh: 渾擊破之，以功封次子尚為關內侯。

translations.literal: Hun struck and broke them; by merit he enfeoffed his second son Shang as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He routed them and enfeoffed his second son Shang as marquis within the passes for the victory.

sentences.zh: 遷安東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事，鎮壽春。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Guards the East, area commander of Yang Province military affairs, garrisoned Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who guards the east, area commander for Yang Province, and stationed at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 吳人大佃皖城，圖為邊害。

translations.literal: The people of Wu carried out large-scale estate farming at Wancheng, intending to become a harm on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wu expanded state farms at Wancheng, plainly aiming to threaten Jin along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 渾遣揚州刺史應綽督淮南諸軍攻破之，並破諸別屯，焚其積穀百八十餘萬斛、稻苗四千餘頃、船六百餘艘。

translations.literal: Hun dispatched Inspector of Yang Province Ying Chuo to supervise the various armies south of the Huai, strike and break them, also breaking the various separate garrisons, burning their stored grain of more than one million eight hundred thousand hu, rice seedling fields of more than four thousand qing, and boats of more than six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun sent provincial inspector Ying Chuo to lead the Huai-south armies against the colony, overrun its outposts, and burn upward of 1.8 million hu of grain, more than four thousand qing of paddy, and over six hundred ships.

sentences.zh: 渾遂陳兵東疆，視其地形險易，曆觀敵城，察攻取之勢。

translations.literal: Hun then arrayed troops on the eastern frontier, inspected whether the terrain was perilous or easy, in turn observed enemy cities, examined the momentum for attack and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: He then massed forces along the eastern border, reconnoitered the ground, toured enemy strongholds, and weighed how they might be taken.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐吳，渾率師出橫江，遣參軍陳慎、都尉張喬攻尋陽瀨鄉，又擊吳牙門將孔忠，皆破之，獲吳將周興等五人。

translations.literal: When there was a great campaign to attack Wu, Hun led the army out from Hengjiang, dispatched staff officer Chen Shen and commandant Zhang Qiao to attack Xunyang Laixiang, also struck Wu gate general Kong Zhong, all were broken, captured Wu generals Zhou Xing and others five men.
translations.idiomatic: In the great offensive against Wu he marched from Hengjiang, sent Chen Shen and Zhang Qiao against Laixiang near Xunyang, defeated Wu gate captain Kong Zhong, and captured five Wu commanders including Zhou Xing.

sentences.zh: 又遣殄吳護軍李純據高望城，討吳將俞恭，破之，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: Also dispatched Extinguish-Wu protector of armies Li Chun to occupy Gaowang city, attacked Wu general Yu Gong, broke him, many beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: He also assigned Li Chun, protector of armies against Wu, to hold Gaowang city, routed the Wu general Yu Gong, and took many heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 吳曆武將軍陳代、平虜將軍硃明懼而來降。

translations.literal: Wu Lü-martial general Chen Dai and pacify-captives general Zhu Ming feared and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Two Wu officers—Chen Dai, a yamen gate general, and Zhu Ming, general who pacifies captives—surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 吳丞相張悌、大將軍孫震等率眾數萬指城陽，渾遣司馬孫疇、揚州刺史周浚擊破之，臨陣斬二將，及首虜七千八百級，吳人大震。

translations.literal: Wu chancellor Zhang Ti, great general Sun Zhen and others led a host of several tens of thousands toward Chengyang; Hun dispatched major Sun Chou, Inspector of Yang Province Zhou Jun to strike and break them, on the battlefield beheaded two generals, and heads and captives seven thousand eight hundred grades; Wu people greatly trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Grand counselor Zhang Ti and Grand General Sun Zhen of Wu advanced tens of thousands of men toward Chengyang; Wang Hun sent Sun Chou and provincial inspector Zhou Jun to crush them, killed two generals on the field, and counted 7,800 heads and prisoners, which shook Wu.

sentences.zh: 孫皓司徒何植、建威將軍孫晏送印節詣渾降。

translations.literal: Sun Hao's minister of education He Zhi, general who establishes might Sun Yan delivered seals and staffs to Hun and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi, Sun Hao's minister of education, and Sun Yan, general who establishes might, brought the seals of office to Wang Hun and capitulated.

sentences.zh: 既而王濬破石頭，降孫皓，威名益振。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Jun broke Shitou, made Sun Hao submit; might name increased further.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Jun took Shitou and forced Sun Hao to surrender, and his own fame grew even louder.

sentences.zh: 明日，渾始濟江，登建鄴宮，釃酒高會。

translations.literal: The next day, Hun for the first time crossed the river, ascended the Jianye palace, strained wine and held a high feast.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wang Hun crossed the Yangzi for the first time, entered the Jianye palaces, and held a grand victory banquet with a libation rite.

sentences.zh: 自以先據江上，破皓中軍，案甲不進，致在王濬之後。

translations.literal: He considered himself first holding the upper river, breaking Hao's central army, resting armor and not advancing, causing him to be behind Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He believed he had seized the middle Yangzi first, shattered Sun Hao's main army, and only then halted—yet that pause had let Wang Jun finish ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 意甚愧恨，有不平之色，頻奏濬罪狀，時人譏之。

translations.literal: Intent very ashamed and resentful, had uneven color, repeatedly memorialized Jun's crimes and conditions; people of the time ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: Burning with humiliation and resentment, he showed it plainly and filed repeated accusations against Wang Jun, and his contemporaries mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔曰：「使持節、都督揚州諸軍事、安東將軍、京陵侯王渾，督率所統，遂逼秣陵，令賊孫皓救死自衛，不得分兵上赴，以成西軍之功，又摧大敵，獲張悌，使皓途窮勢盡，面縛乞降。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying: Bearer of credentials, area commander of Yang Province military affairs, General Who Guards the East, Marquis of Jingling Wang Hun supervised and led what he commanded, pressed up to Moling, made the bandit Sun Hao race to save himself and defend, unable to divide troops and go upstream to the rescue, thereby completing the western army's achievement, also crushed a great enemy, captured Zhang Ti, made Hao road ended and power exhausted, bound with hands behind back begging to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In an edict the emperor praised Wang Hun—credential bearer, Yangzhou area commander, general who guards the east, and marquis of Jingling—for driving on Moling so that Sun Hao could only cling to self-defense and could not send help upstream, completing the western army's mission; for shattering the main enemy, capturing Zhang Ti, and leaving Sun Hao no choice but to come bound and beg surrender.

sentences.zh: 遂平定秣陵，功勳茂著。

translations.literal: Thereupon Moling was pacified; merit and achievement stood luxuriant and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The decree declared that Moling was thereby secured and his achievement resplendent.

sentences.zh: 其增封八千戶，進爵為公，封子澄為亭侯、弟湛為關內侯，賜絹八千匹。

translations.literal: Increase his fief by eight thousand households, advance noble rank to duke, enfeoff son Cheng as village marquis, younger brother Zhan as marquis within the passes, give silk eight thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: It enlarged his fief by eight thousand households, raised his rank to duke, made his son Wang Cheng a precinct marquis and his brother Wang Zhan a marquis within the passes, and awarded eight thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 」轉征東大將軍，復鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: End-quote of speech; he was transferred grand general who conquers the east, again garrisoned Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict he was appointed grand general who conquers the east and again stationed at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 渾不尚刑名，處斷明允。

translations.literal: Hun did not esteem punishments and names; judgments were bright and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun disdained legalistic harshness; his rulings were clear and just.

sentences.zh: 時吳人新附，頗懷畏懼。

translations.literal: At the time Wu people newly attached, quite harbored fear and dread.
translations.idiomatic: The newly submitted people of Wu were still deeply fearful.

sentences.zh: 渾撫循羈旅，虛懷綏納，座無空席，門不停賓。

translations.literal: Hun comforted and guided sojourners, empty bosom pacified and accepted; seats had no empty mats, gate did not stop guests.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun put travelers at ease, welcomed men with genuine openness, kept every seat filled, and turned no caller from his door.

sentences.zh: 於是江東之士莫不悅附。

translations.literal: Thereupon gentlemen east of the river none did not gladly attach.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent east of the Yangzi readily rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 徵拜尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Summoned appointed Deputy Director of the Left of the Secretariat, added regular cavalry attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice director of the left of the secretariat and given the concurrent title of regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 會朝臣立議齊王攸當之籓，渾上書諫曰：「伏承聖詔，憲章古典，進齊王攸為上公，崇其禮儀，遣攸之國。

translations.literal: When court ministers debated that Prince of Qi You ought to go to his fiefdom, Hun submitted a memorial admonishing, saying: I humbly receive the sagely edict, take classical antiquity as model, advance Prince of Qi You to senior duke, exalt his ritual observances, dispatch You to his state.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers argued that Prince Sima You of Qi should be sent to his fief, Wang Hun memorialized in protest: he had heard the decree modeling antiquity, elevating Prince You to senior duke, honoring his rites, and ordering him to his domain.

sentences.zh: 昔周氏建國，大封諸姬，以籓帝室，永世作憲。

translations.literal: Anciently Zhou's clan founded the state, greatly enfeoffed the various Ji, to fence the imperial house, forever making the constitution.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founders built their realm they enfeoffed the house of Ji broadly to screen the throne, and that became the enduring model.

sentences.zh: 至於公旦，武王之弟，左右王事，輔濟大業，不使歸籓。

translations.literal: Reaching Duke of Zhou, a younger brother of King Wu, to the left and right undertook kingly affairs, aided and crossed the great enterprise, did not send him to return to fief.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou—King Wu's brother—stayed at court to manage affairs and help complete the great work instead of being packed off to a domain.

sentences.zh: 明至親義著，不可遠朝故也。

translations.literal: It clarifies that for the closest kin principle is manifest, one cannot distance from court cause.
translations.idiomatic: That shows closest kin whose duty is clear must not be banished from the capital.

sentences.zh: 是故周公得以聖德光弼幼主，忠誠著于《金縢》，光述文武仁聖之德。

translations.literal: Therefore the Duke of Zhou was able with sagely virtue broadly assist the young lord; loyalty appeared in the "Metal-bound Coffer"; he magnified Wen and Wu's benevolent sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Duke of Zhou could nurture the boy king with consummate virtue; his loyalty shines in the "Metal-bound Coffer", and he carried forward the humane wisdom of Kings Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 攸于大晉，姬旦之親也。

translations.literal: You, for great Jin, is Ji Dan's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince You in our Great Jin is the same sort of kinsman as the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 宜贊皇朝，與聞政事，實為陛下腹心不貳之臣。

translations.literal: Should aid the imperial court, participate in hearing government affairs; in truth is Your Majesty's belly-heart not twofold minister.
translations.idiomatic: He ought to support the throne and take part in government; he is, in truth, a trusted minister at your side who will not waver.

sentences.zh: 且攸為人，修潔義信，加以懿親，志存忠貞。

translations.literal: Moreover You as a person is cultivated, pure, righteous, trustworthy, increased by virtue of fine kinship, intent preserving loyalty and steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Prince You is scrupulous, honest, and steadfast, and as your kinsman he is pledged to loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今陛下出攸之國，假以都督虛號，而無典戎幹方之實，去離天朝，不預王政。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty sending You out to his state, lending him area commander's hollow title, yet without the reality of commanding troops and protecting the region, departing and leaving the celestial court, not participating in royal government.
translations.idiomatic: Now you would send him to his fief with only the empty title of area commander and none of the real authority to raise troops or hold a region, cut off from the capital and excluded from governance.

sentences.zh: 傷母弟至親之體，虧友于款篤之義，懼非陛下追述先帝、文明太后待攸之宿意也。

translations.literal: It wounds mother-younger-brother closest kin's body, lacks friends-in Yu warm and thick righteousness, fears it is not Your Majesty's following narrating late emperor, Empress Dowager Wenming's treating You's long-standing intent.
translations.idiomatic: That rends the bond between mother and youngest son, scants the warmth due brothers, and I fear it does not match what the late emperor and Empress Dowager Wenming long meant for Prince You.

sentences.zh: 若以攸望重，於事宜出者，今以汝南王亮代攸。

translations.literal: If because You is weighty in prestige, according to affairs it is fitting he go out, now let Prince of Runan Liang replace You.
translations.idiomatic: If princely stature truly requires someone in the field, appoint Prince Sima Liang of Runan in his place.

sentences.zh: 亮，宣皇帝子，文皇帝弟，伷、駿各處方任，有內外之資，論以後慮，亦不為輕。

translations.literal: Liang is Emperor Xuan's son, Emperor Wen's younger brother; Zhou and Jun each occupy regional charge, have inner and outer resources; discussing by later worries, also is not light.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Liang is a son of Emperor Xuan and younger brother of Emperor Wen, while Sima Zhou and Sima Jun already hold posts inside and outside the court; weighed against long-term concerns, their burden is hardly slight.

sentences.zh: 攸今之國，適足長異同之論，以損仁慈之美耳。

translations.literal: You now going to his state, only suffices to lengthen same-different talk, thereby harming benevolent-kindness's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Banishing Prince You now would only fuel partisan talk and tarnish the grace of your kindness.

sentences.zh: 而令天下窺陛下有不崇親親之情，臣竊為陛下不取也。

translations.literal: Yet it makes the world peer at Your Majesty as having not esteeming kin-on-kin feeling; your subject privately for Your Majesty does not take.
translations.idiomatic: It would let the realm infer that you slight your nearest kin, which I cannot think a wise course.

sentences.zh: 若以妃後外親，任以朝政，則有王氏傾漢之權，呂產專朝之禍。

translations.literal: If because empress's or concubines' outer kin, appoint them to court government, then there is Wang clan overturning Han's power, Lü Chan monopolizing court's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Hand power to in-laws and you invite another Wang Mang who toppled the Han or another Lü Chan who seized the court.

sentences.zh: 若以同姓至親，則有吳楚七國逆亂之殃。

translations.literal: If because same-surname closest kin, then there is Wu-Chu seven states' rebellion and disorder's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fear your own kinsmen and you summon the disaster of the Rebellion of the Seven States.

sentences.zh: 曆觀古今，苟事輕重，所在無不為害也。

translations.literal: Passing through observing ancient and modern, if matters light and heavy, wherever located none do not become harm.
translations.idiomatic: Survey history, high stakes or low: wherever rulers obsess over one danger, harm follows.

sentences.zh: 不可事事曲設疑防，慮方來之患者也。

translations.literal: One cannot in every matter bend to set doubtful defenses, considering what-square-comes's sick.
translations.idiomatic: You cannot invent elaborate precautions for every hypothetical threat.

sentences.zh: 唯當任正道而求忠良。

translations.literal: Only ought to appoint correct way and seek loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: The right path is to uphold just governance and choose loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 若以智計猜物，雖親見疑，至於疏遠者亦何能自保乎！

translations.literal: If by schemes and calculation suspect things, although kin sees suspicion, as for the distant also how can they self-preserve!
translations.idiomatic: If everyone is read through a lens of suspicion, even family looks guilty, and those farther out have no way to feel safe!

sentences.zh: 人懷危懼，非為安之理。

translations.literal: People harboring peril and fear is not for peace's pattern.
translations.idiomatic: A court full of fear is no recipe for stability.

sentences.zh: 此最有國有家者之深忌也。

translations.literal: This is what those who possess a state and possess a house deeply taboo.
translations.idiomatic: That is the deepest fear of anyone who holds a throne or a household.

sentences.zh: 愚以為太子太保缺，宜留攸居之，與太尉汝南王亮、衛將軍楊珧共為保傅，幹理朝事。

translations.literal: Foolishly I think the heir's junior tutor is vacant; it is fitting to retain You dwelling in it, together with Grand Commandant Prince of Runan Liang, Defender-in-chief Yang Yao jointly be protectors and tutors, manage and order court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the junior tutor to the crown prince stands open: keep Prince You in that office, share the guardians' college with Grand Commandant Sima Liang and Defender Yang Yao, and let them jointly steer the ministries.

sentences.zh: 三人齊位，足相持正，進有輔納廣義之益，退無偏重相傾之勢。

translations.literal: Three men equal rank, sufficient mutually uphold correctness; advancing has assisting and receiving broad righteousness's benefit; retiring has no one side heavy mutually toppling momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Three peers can balance one another—gaining breadth of counsel without letting any faction grow heavy enough to overturn the rest.

sentences.zh: 令陛下有篤親親之恩，使攸蒙仁覆之惠。

translations.literal: Order Your Majesty have thick kin-on-kin grace, make You receive benevolent covering's favor.
translations.idiomatic: You would show devotion to kin while Prince You still enjoys your sheltering favor.

sentences.zh: 臣同國休戚，義在盡言，心之所見，不能默已。

translations.literal: Your subject shares state's weal and woe; right lies in exhausting words; what the heart sees, cannot be silent already.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant shares the dynasty's fortunes and must speak his mind; I cannot hold this back.

sentences.zh: 私慕魯女存國之志，敢陳愚見，觸犯天威。

translations.literal: Privately admiring Lu maiden's preserving state's intent, dare present foolish view, offending heavenly might.
translations.idiomatic: Like the women of Lu who spoke to save their state, I risk my foolish counsel though it offends your majesty.

sentences.zh: 欲陛下事每盡善，冀萬分之助。

translations.literal: Desiring Your Majesty's affairs each reach utmost good, hope for ten-thousandth-part's aid.
translations.idiomatic: I wish every decision of yours to be for the best and offer this mite of help.

sentences.zh: 臣而不言，誰當言者。

translations.literal: Your subject if not speaking, who ought to speak.
translations.idiomatic: If I as your servant keep silent, who is fit to speak up.

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: End-quote of speech; the emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the plea.

sentences.zh: 太熙初，遷司徒。

translations.literal: Early in Taixi, promoted minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taixi he became minister of education.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，加侍中，又京陵置士官，如睢陵比。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended, added palace attendant, also for Jingling placed officers-of-works, as Suiling comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui he was also named palace attendant, and a corps of artisan officers was assigned to his Jingling estate on the model used at Suiling.

sentences.zh: 及誅楊駿，崇重舊臣，乃加渾兵。

translations.literal: When they executed Yang Jun, exalted and weighted old ministers, then added troops to Hun.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun's purge the court honored elder statesmen and authorized Wang Hun to retain armed guards.

sentences.zh: 渾以司徒文官，主史不持兵，持兵乃吏屬絳衣。

translations.literal: Hun, as minister of education civil official, chief clerk did not hold arms; holding arms then was subordinate clerks' crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of education he was a civil officer whose chief registrar bore no arms; armed attendants were crimson-clad staff under him.

sentences.zh: 自以偶因時寵，權得持兵，非是舊典，皆令皁服。

translations.literal: He considered himself accidentally by the time's favor, by power obtained holding arms, not the old standard, all ordered black robes.
translations.idiomatic: He knew his guards were an unusual favor, not precedent, and had them all dress in black instead of crimson.

sentences.zh: 論者美其謙而識體。

translations.literal: Discussers praised his modesty and understanding of body/propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators admired his humility and sense of decorum.

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋將害汝南王亮等也。

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Wei was about to harm Prince of Runan Liang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Wei of Chu was plotting to kill Sima Liang of Runan and the other princes.

sentences.zh: 公孫宏說瑋曰：「昔宣帝廢曹爽，引太尉蔣濟參乘，以增威重。

translations.literal: Gongsun Hong persuaded Wei saying: Anciently Emperor Xuan deposed Cao Shuang, brought Grand Commandant Jiang Ji to ride in the same carriage, to increase awesome weight.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong told Sima Wei that Emperor Xuan had shared a carriage with Grand Commandant Jiang Ji when he moved against Cao Shuang, the better to lend the act authority.

sentences.zh: 大王今舉非常事，宜得宿望，鎮厭眾心。

translations.literal: Great king now raises an extraordinary affair; it is fitting to obtain old standing prestige, press down the multitude's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: A coup of this kind required a veteran whose prestige would steady the troops.

sentences.zh: 司徒王渾宿有威名，為三軍所信服，可請同乘，使物情有憑也。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Hun long has awesome name, is believed and submitted to by the three armies; can invite same carriage, make things' sentiment have reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Hun commanded the armies' trust; inviting him to ride along would reassure the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」瑋從之。

translations.literal: End-quote of speech; Wei followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wei agreed.

sentences.zh: 渾辭疾歸第，以家兵千餘人閉門距瑋。

translations.literal: Hun declined illness and returned to his mansion, with household troops over a thousand men closed gate and resisted Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun pleaded illness, retired home, and barred his gates with more than a thousand family retainers against Sima Wei.

sentences.zh: 瑋不敢逼。

translations.literal: Wei did not dare press.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wei dared not force him.

sentences.zh: 俄而瑋以矯詔伏誅，渾乃率兵赴官。

translations.literal: Soon Wei because forged edict was executed lying prostrate; Hun then led troops proceeding to office.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Wei was quickly executed for forging an edict, Wang Hun marched his men back to duty.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗訪渾元會問郡國計吏方俗之宜，渾奏曰：「陛下欽明聖哲，光於遠近，明詔沖虛，詢及芻蕘，斯乃周文疇咨之求，仲尼不恥下問也。

translations.literal: The emperor once consulted Hun at New Year assembly about commandery-state accounting clerks and regional customs' fitness; Hun memorial-replied saying: Your Majesty reverent-bright sagely wise, radiance toward far and near, bright edict empty-modest, inquire reaching firewood-gatherers, this then is Zhou Wen's planning-consultation seeking, Zhongni not shamed lower asking.
translations.idiomatic: At a New Year court the emperor asked Wang Hun how provincial accounting officers should be examined on local ways. Hun replied that the sovereign's luminous edict already sought advice even from common woodcutters, in the spirit of King Wen's wide consultation and Confucius's readiness to learn from anyone.

sentences.zh: 舊三朝元會前計吏詣軒下，侍中讀詔，計吏跪受。

translations.literal: Old: before the three-court New Year assembly accounting clerks proceeded under the carriage eaves, attendant-in-ordinary read the edict, accounting clerks knelt and received.
translations.idiomatic: By long custom, before the triple audience on New Year's day the clerks came below the gallery, an attendant-in-ordinary read the proclamation aloud, and they knelt to receive it.

sentences.zh: 臣以詔文相承已久，無他新聲，非陛下留心方國之意也。

translations.literal: Your subject considers the edict's text succeeding one another already long, without other new sound, not Your Majesty giving heart to commandery-states' intent.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the formula has been recited unchanged for ages; it no longer shows that you truly care about conditions in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 可令中書指宣明詔，問方土異同，賢才秀異，風俗好尚，農桑本務，刑獄得無冤濫，守長得無侵虐。

translations.literal: Can order the secretariat point proclaim bright edict, ask regional soil same-difference, worthy talents outstanding excellence, customs likes and esteem, agriculture-mulberry root tasks, punishments and prisons obtain none wrongful excess, guardians and chiefs obtain none encroach cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Let the secretariat issue an explicit mandate asking about regional differences, notable talent, popular customs, farming and sericulture, whether justice is free of abuse, and whether prefects oppress the people.

sentences.zh: 其勤心政化興利除害者，授以紙筆，盡意陳聞。

translations.literal: As for those who diligently attend to government, promote benefit, and remove harm, give them paper and brush so they may set out their views in full.
translations.idiomatic: Give brush and paper to any who labor at good government so they can set out their views in full.

sentences.zh: 以明聖指垂心四遠，不復因循常辭。

translations.literal: Thereby clarify sagely finger lowering heart to four distances, no longer follow along usual phrases.
translations.idiomatic: That would show your concern reaches the farthest corners of the realm instead of recycling empty phrases.

sentences.zh: 且察其答對文義，以觀計吏人才之實。

translations.literal: Moreover inspect their answer-reply text meaning, thereby observe accounting clerks' human talent's reality.
translations.idiomatic: Their answers would also reveal how capable these officers really are.

sentences.zh: 又先帝時，正會後東堂見征鎮長史司馬、諸王國卿、諸州別駕。

translations.literal: Moreover under the late emperor, after the main assembly the Eastern Hall saw campaign-garrison senior scribes and majors, various princely state ministers, various provinces' chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Under the late emperor, after the great audience he received in the Eastern Hall the senior staff of field commands, ministers of princely estates, and provincial chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 今若不能別見，可前詣軒下，使侍中宣問，以審察方國，於事為便。

translations.literal: Now if cannot separate audience, can beforehand proceed to under carriage eaves, let attendant-in-ordinary proclaim ask, thereby carefully inspect commandery-states, in affairs is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: If a separate audience is impractical, let them advance below the carriage porch while an attendant-in-ordinary poses your questions—an efficient way to learn about the provinces.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: End-quote of speech; the emperor assented to it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又詔渾錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Also edict Hun record Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was further ordered to supervise the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 渾所曆之職，前後著稱，及居台輔，聲望日減。

translations.literal: The offices Hun passed through, before and after enjoyed reputation; reaching occupying terrace assistants, fame and prestige daily diminished.
translations.idiomatic: He had won praise in every post until he reached the chancellorship; there his reputation slowly waned.

sentences.zh: 薨，時年七十五，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Passed away, at the time age seventy-five, posthumous name said Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five and received the posthumous epithet Yuan.

sentences.zh: 長子尚早亡，次子濟嗣。

translations.literal: Eldest son Shang died early; second son Ji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shang died young; the second son, Ji, inherited his title.

translations.literal: The source text prints a line of equals signs as a section divider.

sentences.zh: 子濟

translations.literal: Zi Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji

sentences.zh: =濟字武子。

translations.literal: The source text prefixes a rule line to: Ji, courtesy name Wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, whose courtesy name was Wuzi,

sentences.zh: 少有逸才，風姿英爽，氣蓋一時，好弓馬，勇力絕人，善《易》及《莊》、《老》，文詞俊茂，伎藝過人，有名當世，與姊夫和嶠及裴楷齊名。

translations.literal: In youth he had escaping talent, bearing and mien heroic and bright, spirit overshadowed the age, loved bow and horse, courage and strength surpassed others, was good at the "Changes", the "Zhuangzi", and the "Laozi", literary phrasing handsome and lush, craft and skill passed others, had fame in the age, with brother-in-law He Jiao and Pei Kai equally named.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he showed rare ability, carried himself with dash, and towered over his generation; he excelled at riding and archery, possessed uncanny strength, mastered the "Book of Changes", the "Zhuangzi", and the "Laozi", and wrote with panache; his arts outclassed others, and he stood alongside his brother-in-law He Jiao and Pei Kai.

sentences.zh: 尚常山公主。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Princess of Changshan as his wife.

sentences.zh: 年二十，起家拜中書郎，以母憂去官。

translations.literal: At twenty he first rose from family rank as gentleman of the palace secretariat, then left office for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered service as a gentleman of the palace secretariat but resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 起為驍騎將軍，累遷侍中，與侍中孔恂、王恂、楊濟同列，為一時秀彥。

translations.literal: He was recalled as general of fierce cavalry, promoted in stages to palace attendant, serving together with attendants Kong Xun, Wang Xun, and Yang Ji as the day's leading talents.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as general of fierce cavalry, he rose to palace attendant alongside Kong Xun, Wang Xun, and Yang Ji—the outstanding men of the moment.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗會公卿籓牧於式乾殿，顧濟、恂而謂諸公曰：「朕左右可謂恂恂濟濟矣！

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once assembled high ministers and frontier shepherds in Shiqian Hall, looked toward Ji and Xun and said to the lords: "Those at my side may truly be called orderly and abundant!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once gathered ministers and regional commanders in Shiqian Hall, glanced at Wang Ji and Kong Xun, and told the assembly, "My attendants are a model of dignity and talent!"—punning on their names.

sentences.zh: 」每侍見，未嘗不諮論人物及萬機得失。

translations.literal: End-quote; every time he attended audience there was never a session without weighing men and the gains and losses of state business.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended court, the emperor consulted him on character and policy without fail.

sentences.zh: 濟善於清言，修飾辭令，諷議將順，朝臣莫能尚焉。

translations.literal: Ji was skilled in pure conversation, polished his phrasing, offered tactful advice that followed the ruler's mood, and no minister could surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at Qingtan debate, shaped his words with care, and gave supple counsel that none at court could match.

sentences.zh: 帝益親貴之。

translations.literal: The emperor drew closer to him and honored him more.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign came to favor him ever more warmly.

sentences.zh: 仕進雖速，論者不以主婿之故，咸謂才能致之。

translations.literal: Though his promotions came quickly, critics did not attribute it to his status as imperial son-in-law; all said talent had won the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Even his rapid rise was credited to ability rather than marriage into the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 然外雖弘雅，而內多忌刻，好以言傷物，儕類以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet outwardly grand and refined, inwardly he was jealous and harsh, loved wounding others with words, and peers thought less of him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the polish he was jealous and cutting, prone to barbed speech, and contemporaries quietly disdained him.

sentences.zh: 以其父之故，每排王濬，時議譏焉。

translations.literal: Because of his father's quarrel he repeatedly slighted Wang Jun, and opinion at court ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: He kept needling Wang Jun over his father's feud, and observers mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸當之籓，濟既陳請，又累使公主與甄德妻長廣公主俱入，稽顙泣請帝留攸。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi You was ordered to his fief, Ji had already petitioned; he also repeatedly sent the princess with Zhen De's wife, the Princess of Changuang, into the palace to kowtow and weep, begging the emperor to keep You.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince Sima You of Qi was sent away, Wang Ji had memorialized in vain; he then sent his wife and Zhen De's spouse, the Princess of Changuang, to throw themselves before the throne weeping, pleading that You be allowed to stay.

sentences.zh: 帝怒謂侍中王戎曰：「兄弟至親，今出齊王，自是朕家事，而甄德、王濟連遣婦來生哭人！

translations.literal: The emperor angrily told attendant Wang Rong: "Brothers are closest kin; expelling Prince of Qi is my household affair, yet Zhen De and Wang Ji keep sending their wives to harass me with wailing!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped to Wang Rong, "Brothers are family; banishing Prince of Qi is my decision, yet Zhen De and Wang Ji keep dispatching their wives to shame me with public tears!"

sentences.zh: 」以忤旨，左遷國子祭酒，常侍如故。

translations.literal: End-quote; for offending the ruler he was shifted left to libationer of the imperial academy, keeping his title of regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For the affront he was demoted to libationer of the imperial academy while retaining his regular attendant's rank.

sentences.zh: 數年，入為侍中。

translations.literal: After several years he returned as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he was back at court as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時渾為僕射，主者處事或不當，濟性峻厲，明法繩之。

translations.literal: At the time Hun was vice director; when staff decisions went awry Ji's stern nature applied the statutes strictly.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Hun served as vice director of the secretariat, Wang Ji enforced the rules ruthlessly whenever clerks erred.

sentences.zh: 素與從兄佑不平，佑黨頗謂濟不能顧其父，由是長同異之言。

translations.literal: He had long clashed with his cousin You; You's faction said Ji failed to honor his father, feeding factional gossip.
translations.idiomatic: He was estranged from his cousin Wang You, whose followers claimed he dishonored his father—fuel for partisan sniping.

sentences.zh: 出為河南尹，未拜，坐鞭王官吏免官。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Henan but before investiture was stripped of office for flogging a prince's household officer.
translations.idiomatic: Named governor of Henan, he lost the post before taking it because he had whipped an official of a princely household.

sentences.zh: 而王佑始見委任。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Wang You began to win real responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang You started to gain substantive appointments.

sentences.zh: 而濟遂被斥外，於是乃移第北芒山下。

translations.literal: Ji was cast to the margins and moved his mansion to the foot of Mount Mang north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Pushed to the sidelines, he relocated his residence below Mount Mang north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 性豪侈，麗服玉食。

translations.literal: His nature was proud and extravagant, with splendid dress and jade-bright fare.
translations.idiomatic: He lived ostentatiously, draped in finery and dining like a king.

sentences.zh: 時洛京地甚貴，濟買地為馬埒，編錢滿之，時人謂為「金溝」。

translations.literal: Luoyang land was costly; Ji bought a plot for a horse course and paved it with strings of cash; people called it the "Gold Ditch."
translations.idiomatic: When capital real estate was ruinously expensive, he bought land for a riding ring and carpeted it with coins—onlookers dubbed the place the "Gold Ditch."

sentences.zh: 王愷以帝舅奢豪，有牛名「八百里駁」，常瑩其蹄角。

translations.literal: Wang Kai, the emperor's uncle by marriage, kept a famously rich household and an ox named "Eight-hundred-li Piebald," and he buffed its hooves and horns.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai, the sovereign's maternal uncle, flaunted his wealth with an ox called "Eight-hundred-li Piebald," always polishing its hooves and horns.

sentences.zh: 濟請以錢千萬與牛對射而賭之。

translations.literal: Ji offered ten million cash to wager on archery against the beast.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji staked ten million cash on an archery contest against the animal.

sentences.zh: 愷亦自恃其能，令濟先射。

translations.literal: Kai trusted his own skill and let Ji shoot first.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai, confident in his marksmanship, let Wang Ji open the round.

sentences.zh: 一發破的，因據胡床，叱左右速探牛心來，須臾而至，一割便去。

translations.literal: One shot pierced the target; he seized a folding stool, barked at attendants to cut out the ox's heart, and in moments it arrived; he carved once and walked off.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji shattered the target in one shot, dropped onto a camp stool, ordered servants to fetch the ox's heart, carved a single slice when it came, and left.

sentences.zh: 和嶠性至儉，家有好李，帝求之，不過數十。

translations.literal: He Jiao was extremely frugal and kept fine plums; when the emperor asked for some he sent only a few dozen.
translations.idiomatic: He Jiao, a miser, grew excellent plums yet sent the emperor only a handful when asked.

sentences.zh: 濟候其上直，率少年詣園，共啖畢，伐樹而去。

translations.literal: Ji waited until He went on palace duty, led youths to the orchard, ate every plum together, then felled the tree and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji waited for He Jiao's palace shift, stormed the garden with young companions, devoured the crop, chopped the tree down, and departed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗幸其宅，供饌甚豐，悉貯琉璃器中。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited his house; the feast was lavish and every dish stood in glass vessels.
translations.idiomatic: On an imperial visit his table glittered with crystal vessels and extravagant dishes.

sentences.zh: 蒸肫甚美，帝問其故，答曰：「以人乳蒸之。

translations.literal: The steamed gizzard was superb; asked the secret, he replied: "It was steamed with human milk."
translations.idiomatic: The steamed gizzards were exquisite; asked how, he answered coolly, "Human milk."

sentences.zh: 」帝色甚不平，食未畢而去。

translations.literal: End-quote; the emperor's look turned dark and he left before finishing the meal.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's face darkened and he quit the meal unfinished.

sentences.zh: 濟善解馬性，嘗乘一馬，著連乾鄣泥，前有水，終不肯渡。

translations.literal: Ji understood horses; riding one saddled with linked mud-guards, he halted before water and would not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji read horses well; once, riding a mount in layered mud-flaps, he stopped short of a stream and refused to ford.

sentences.zh: 濟云：「此必是惜鄣泥。

translations.literal: Ji said: "It must be sparing the mud-guards."
translations.idiomatic: "It fears ruining the mud-flaps," he said.

sentences.zh: 」使人解去，便渡。

translations.literal: End-quote; he had men strip them off and the horse crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Men removed the guards and the horse crossed at once.

sentences.zh: 故杜預謂濟有馬癖。

translations.literal: Hence Du Yu said Ji had a horse obsession.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu joked that Wang Ji was horse-mad.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂和嶠曰：「我將罵濟而後官爵之，何如？

translations.literal: The emperor once told He Jiao: "I mean to berate Ji before ennobling him; what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked He Jiao whether he should humiliate Wang Ji before granting him honors.

sentences.zh: 」嶠曰：「濟俊爽，恐不可屈。

translations.literal: End-quote; Jiao said: "Ji is proud and bright; I fear he cannot be bent."
translations.idiomatic: He Jiao replied that Wang Ji was too proud to endure a public scolding.

sentences.zh: 」帝因召濟，切讓之，既而曰：「知愧不？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Ji, rebuked him sharply, then asked: "Do you feel shame?"
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign called him in, dressed him down, then demanded, "Are you ashamed?"

sentences.zh: 」濟答曰：「尺布鬥粟之謠，常為陛下恥之。

translations.literal: End-quote; Ji answered: "The ballad of a foot of cloth and a peck of grain—your servant has long been ashamed for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji answered, "The old ballad about brothers who starved each other shames me for you, sire."

sentences.zh: 他人能令親疏，臣不能使親親，以此愧陛下耳。

translations.literal: Others may widen the gap between kin; your servant cannot make kin love kin; with that I shame Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Other men may set kin against kin; I cannot make brothers cherish one another—that is how I shame you.

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: End-quote; the emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與濟弈棋，而孫皓在側，謂皓曰：「何以好剝人面皮？

translations.literal: The emperor once played chess with Ji while Sun Hao stood by and asked Hao: "Why did you like flaying men's faces?"
translations.idiomatic: Playing weiqi with Wang Ji while Sun Hao watched, the emperor asked the former Wu ruler why he had enjoyed facial flaying.

sentences.zh: 」皓曰：「見無禮於君者則剝之。

translations.literal: End-quote; Hao said: "When I saw someone rude to his lord I flayed him."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao answered that he had only punished subjects who were rude to their ruler.

sentences.zh: 」濟時伸腳局下，而皓譏焉。

translations.literal: End-quote; Ji had stretched his feet beneath the board, and Hao used it to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji had his legs stretched under the board—Sun Hao's barb implied he was the rude subject.

sentences.zh: 尋使白衣領太僕。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to oversee the Minister of Carriages in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made to direct the Minister of Carriages while still in disgraced white robes.

sentences.zh: 年四十六，先渾卒，追贈驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: At forty-six he died before Hun; he was posthumously named general of swift cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-six, predeceasing his father, and was posthumously honored as general of swift cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及其將葬，時賢無不畢至。

translations.literal: When the burial neared, every notable of the day attended.
translations.idiomatic: As the funeral approached, the elite of the capital all gathered.

sentences.zh: 孫楚雅敬濟，而後來，哭之甚悲，賓客莫不垂涕。

translations.literal: Sun Chu deeply respected Ji but arrived late, wept him bitterly, and guests all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu revered him, came late, and wept so bitterly that the mourners wept with him.

sentences.zh: 哭畢，向靈床曰：「卿常好我作驢鳴，我為卿作之。

translations.literal: When the weeping ended he told the bier: "You always liked me to bray like a donkey; I bray for you."
translations.idiomatic: When the lament ended he told the corpse, "You loved my donkey bray; hear it now."

sentences.zh: 」體似聲真，賓客皆笑。

translations.literal: End-quote; his posture matched the sound so well the guests laughed.
translations.idiomatic: His mimicry was perfect and the mourners laughed despite themselves.

sentences.zh: 楚顧曰：「諸君不死，而令王濟死乎！」

translations.literal: Chu looked about and said: "You gentlemen are not dead yet, yet you let Wang Ji die!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu glared around and cried, "You still live while Wang Ji lies dead?"

sentences.zh: 初，濟尚主，主兩目失明，而妒忌尤甚，然終無子，有庶子二人。

translations.literal: At first, when Ji married the princess, she was blind in both eyes and fiercely jealous, yet bore no sons, though two sons were born to concubines.
translations.idiomatic: The princess he married was blind and fiercely jealous, bore no heir, yet accepted two sons by concubines.

sentences.zh: 卓字文宣，嗣渾爵，拜給事中。

translations.literal: Zhuo, courtesy name Wenxuan, succeeded to Hun's noble rank and was appointed gentleman attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo, courtesy name Wenxuan, inherited Wang Hun's title and became a gentleman attendant.

sentences.zh: 次聿，字茂宣，襲公主封敏陽侯。

translations.literal: The second, Yu, courtesy name Maoxuan, inherited the princess's fief as marquis of Minyang.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son Wang Yu, courtesy name Maoxuan, took the princess's estate as marquis of Minyang.

sentences.zh: 濟二弟，澄字道深，汶字茂深，皆辯慧有才藻，並曆清顯。

translations.literal: Ji's two younger brothers Cheng, courtesy name Daoshen, and Wen, courtesy name Maoshen, were clever, literary, and each rose to eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Wang Cheng and Wang Wen—courtesy names Daoshen and Maoshen—were gifted writers who climbed to high office.

sentences.zh: 王濬

translations.literal: Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun

sentences.zh: 王濬，字士治，弘農湖人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, courtesy name Shizhi, was a man of Hu in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, whose courtesy name was Shizhi, came from Hu in Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世二千石。

translations.literal: For generations his family held two-thousand-bushel rank.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had held ministerial-grade salaries for generations.

sentences.zh: 濬博墳典，美姿貌，不修名行，不為鄉曲所稱。

translations.literal: Jun read widely in the classics, was handsome in appearance, did not cultivate reputation or conduct, and won no praise in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He read deeply and looked striking, yet neglected reputation and local opinion thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 晚乃變節，疏通亮達，恢廓有大志。

translations.literal: Only later did he change course, becoming open, candid, and ambitious on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: Later he remade himself—forthright, far-seeing, and hungry for great things.

sentences.zh: 嘗起宅，開門前路廣數十步。

translations.literal: Once building a house he cleared a roadway dozens of paces wide before the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Building a manor, he carved a boulevard tens of paces wide outside his gate.

sentences.zh: 人或謂之何太過，濬曰：「吾欲使容長戟幡旗。

translations.literal: People said it was excessive; Jun replied: "I mean to leave room for long halberds and banner poles."
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors mocked the extravagance; he said he needed space for halberds and banners.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸笑之，濬曰：「陳勝有言，燕雀安知鴻鵠之志。

translations.literal: End-quote; all laughed; Jun said: "Chen Sheng said swallows and sparrows cannot know the wild swan's mind."
translations.idiomatic: They laughed; he quoted Chen Sheng—sparrows cannot grasp a swan's aim.

sentences.zh: 」州郡辟河東從事。

translations.literal: End-quote; provinces summoned him as a clerk in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was hired as a clerk in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 守令有不廉潔者，皆望風自引而去。

translations.literal: Magistrates who were corrupt caught wind and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Dishonest county magistrates fled at word of his arrival.

sentences.zh: 刺史燕國徐邈有女才淑，擇夫未嫁。

translations.literal: Inspector Xu Miao of Yan had a talented, virtuous daughter still unbetrothed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao, inspector of Yan, had a gifted daughter who had found no husband.

sentences.zh: 邈乃大會佐吏，令女於內觀之。

translations.literal: Miao convened his staff and had her watch them from within.
translations.idiomatic: He assembled his aides and let her observe them from behind a screen.

sentences.zh: 女指濬告母，邈遂妻之。

translations.literal: The daughter pointed to Jun and told her mother; Miao married her to him.
translations.idiomatic: She chose Wang Jun; Xu Miao gave her to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 後參征南軍事，羊祜深知待之。

translations.literal: Later he joined the staff of the southern expedition; Yang Hu valued him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on the southern campaign staff, where Yang Hu became his steadfast patron.

sentences.zh: 祜兄子暨白祜：「濬為人志太，奢侈不節，不可專任，宜有以裁之。

translations.literal: Hu's nephew Ji told Hu: "Jun's ambition is too large and his spending unbridled; do not rely on him alone—rein him in."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji's nephew warned that Wang Jun's ambition and extravagance required restraint, not sole command.

sentences.zh: 」祜曰：「濬有大才，將欲濟其所欲，必可用也。

translations.literal: End-quote; Hu said: "Jun has great talent; to achieve his aims he must be used."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu replied that great gifts like Wang Jun's had to be harnessed, not clipped.

sentences.zh: 」轉車騎從事中郎，識者謂祜可謂能舉善焉。

translations.literal: End-quote; transferred attendant clerk of chariot cavalry; observers said Hu knew how to lift good men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun moved to the chariot and cavalry command staff, and onlookers praised Yang Hu for promoting talent.

sentences.zh: 除巴郡太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He became governor of Ba.

sentences.zh: 郡邊吳境，兵士苦役，生男多不養。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered Wu; soldiers groaned under labor levies and often refused to rear sons.
translations.idiomatic: Hard service on the Wu frontier led families to abandon newborn boys.

sentences.zh: 濬乃嚴其科條，寬其徭課，其產育者皆與休復，所全活者數千人。

translations.literal: Jun tightened statutes, eased corvée and taxes, granted rest to parents of newborns, and saved several thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: He stiffened the law but lightened taxes, rewarded child-rearing, and kept thousands of infants alive.

sentences.zh: 轉廣漢太守，垂惠布政，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guanghan, he spread kindness in government and the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Guanghan he ruled with mercy and won the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 濬夜夢懸三刀於臥屋梁上，須臾又益一刀，濬警覺，意甚惡之。

translations.literal: Jun dreamed three knives hung on his bedchamber beam; soon a fourth appeared; he woke alarmed and thought it ill.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of three knives on his rafters, then a fourth—he woke uneasy.

sentences.zh: 主簿李毅再拜賀曰：「三刀為州字，又益一者，明府其臨益州乎？

translations.literal: Chief clerk Li Yi bowed twice and said: "Three knives form the character 'province'; adding one means my lord will govern Yi Province?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Li Yi hailed it as an omen: three blades make the graph for "province," and a fourth foretold the Yizhou post.

sentences.zh: 」及賊張弘殺益州刺史皇甫晏，果遷濬為益州刺史。

translations.literal: End-quote; when rebel Zhang Hong slew Inspector Huangfu Yan, Jun was indeed promoted inspector of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hong murdered Inspector Huangfu Yan, Wang Jun was raised to inspector of Yi as foretold.

sentences.zh: 濬設方略，悉誅弘等，以勳封關內侯。

translations.literal: Jun planned operations, executed Hong and his party, and was enfeoffed marquis within the passes for merit.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted the strike, eliminated Zhang Hong's band, and earned a marquisate within the passes.

sentences.zh: 懷輯殊俗，待以威信，蠻夷徼外，多來歸降。

translations.literal: He soothed alien peoples with trust and awe; many tribes beyond the frontier submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He won border peoples with authority and grace until many tribes surrendered.

sentences.zh: 徵拜右衛將軍，除大司農。

translations.literal: Summoned as general of the right guard, appointed minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as general of the right guard and named minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍羊祜雅知濬有奇略，乃密表留濬，於是重拜益州刺史。

translations.literal: General of chariots Yang Hu knew Jun's strategy; he secretly memorialized to keep him, so Jun was again inspector of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu, general of chariots, grasped his strategic mind and secured a second appointment as inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 武帝謀伐吳，詔濬修舟艦。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu planned the Wu campaign he ordered Jun to build warships.
translations.idiomatic: Planning the conquest of Wu, Emperor Wu told Wang Jun to construct a river fleet.

sentences.zh: 濬乃作大船連舫，方百二十步，受二千餘人。

translations.literal: Jun built linked barges a hundred twenty paces square holding more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He built massive linked hulls, each deck a hundred twenty paces square and carrying over two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 以木為城，起樓櫓，開四出門，其上皆得馳馬來往。

translations.literal: Wood palisades rose like city walls with watchtowers and four gates; horsemen could gallop the decks.
translations.idiomatic: Timber ramparts and towered parapets ringed them with four gates where riders could charge.

sentences.zh: 又畫鷁首怪獸於船首，以懼江神。

translations.literal: He painted demon-faced figureheads to overawe the river spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Fearsome figureheads were painted to cow the river gods.

sentences.zh: 舟楫之盛，自古未有。

translations.literal: Never had shipping been so grand.
translations.idiomatic: No fleet in memory matched their scale.

sentences.zh: 濬造船於蜀，其木柿蔽江而下。

translations.literal: Building in Shu, he floated scrap wood downriver until it choked the current.
translations.idiomatic: Shipwrights in Shu sent so much scrap timber downstream that it carpeted the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 吳建平太守吾彥取流柿以呈孫皓曰：「晉必有攻吳之計，宜增建平兵。

translations.literal: Wu governor Wu Yan caught the driftwood and told Sun Hao: "Jin surely plans to strike Wu; reinforce Jianping."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan, Wu's governor of Jianping, fished out the chips and warned Sun Hao that Jin was preparing war and Jianping must be strengthened.

sentences.zh: 建平不下，終不敢渡。

translations.literal: If Jianping does not fall they will never dare cross.
translations.idiomatic: While Jianping holds, the enemy cannot risk a crossing.

sentences.zh: 」皓不從。

translations.literal: End-quote; Hao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 尋以謠言拜濬為龍驤將軍、監梁益諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon a prophecy led to Jun's appointment as dragon-leaping general overseeing Liang and Yi forces.
translations.idiomatic: Court prophecy soon made Wang Jun dragon-leaping general with command over Liang and Yi.

sentences.zh: 語在《羊祜傳》。

translations.literal: The account appears in the "Biography of Yang Hu".
translations.idiomatic: The fuller story is told in Yang Hu's biography.

sentences.zh: 時朝議咸諫伐吳，濬乃上疏曰：「臣數參訪吳楚同異，孫皓荒淫凶逆，荊揚賢愚無不嗟怨。

translations.literal: When courtiers all urged against attacking Wu, Jun memorialized: "Your servant has often compared Wu and Chu; Sun Hao is dissolute and cruel, and worthies and fools alike in Jing and Yang groan under him."
translations.idiomatic: While ministers counseled delay, Wang Jun argued that Sun Hao's tyranny had turned Jing and Yang against him.

sentences.zh: 且觀時運，宜速征伐。

translations.literal: Moreover the times call for swift campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: The moment favored a rapid strike.

sentences.zh: 若今不伐，天變難預。

translations.literal: If we do not attack now, heaven's shifts cannot be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Wait, and celestial fortune may turn against us.

sentences.zh: 令皓卒死，更立賢主，文武各得其所，則強敵也。

translations.literal: If Hao dies suddenly and a worthy ruler arises so civil and military talent each finds its place, Wu becomes a formidable foe.
translations.idiomatic: If Sun Hao died and a capable successor reorganized Wu, the south would become a stubborn enemy.

sentences.zh: 臣作船七年，日有朽敗，又臣年已七十，死亡無日。

translations.literal: Your subject has built ships seven years; daily they rot; moreover your subject is seventy and death is near.
translations.idiomatic: I have spent seven years on this fleet; timbers rot daily; I am seventy and time is short.

sentences.zh: 三者一乖，則難圖也，誠願陛下無失事機。

translations.literal: If those three once part ways, then it is hard to plan; I sincerely wish Your Majesty not to miss the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: Lose any one of those three advantages and the campaign becomes doubtful; I beg you not to let this chance slip.

sentences.zh: 」帝深納焉。

translations.literal: End-quote; the emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 賈充、荀勖陳諫以為不可，唯張華固勸。

translations.literal: Jia Chong and Xun Xu argued against it, deeming the time wrong; only Zhang Hua pressed the case.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong and Xun Xu counseled delay, while Zhang Hua alone urged war.

sentences.zh: 又杜預表請，帝乃發詔，分命諸方節度。

translations.literal: Du Yu also memorialized in request; the emperor then issued an edict, dividing orders among the regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu weighed in as well, so the throne issued orders splintering command among the fronts.

sentences.zh: 濬於是統兵。

translations.literal: Jun then took overall command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun assumed field command.

sentences.zh: 先在巴郡之所全育者，皆堪徭役供軍，其父母戒之曰：「王府君生爾，爾必勉之，無愛死也！」

translations.literal: Those whom he had earlier spared and raised in Ba commandery could all bear corvée and supply the army; their parents admonished them, saying: "Lord Wang gave you life; you must strive hard; do not cling to life!"
translations.idiomatic: The youths Wang Jun had saved in Ba could now serve; their parents told them, "The inspector gave you life—fight without sparing yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 正月，濬發自成都，率巴東監軍、廣武將軍唐彬攻吳丹楊，克之，擒其丹楊監盛紀。

translations.literal: In the first month Jun set out from Chengdu, leading Ba-East overseer of armies and Guangwu general Tang Bin against Wu's Danyang, took it, and captured Danyang overseer Sheng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: That month he left Chengdu with Tang Bin, seized Wu's Danyang, and took its governor Sheng Ji.

sentences.zh: 吳人于江險磧要害之處，並以鐵鎖橫截之，又作鐵錐長丈餘，暗置江中，以逆距船。

translations.literal: Wu men at the river's perilous shallows and choke points stretched iron chains to block the channel and forged iron spikes over a zhang long, hiding them in the current to impede ships.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders chained the narrows and seeded the bed with yard-long iron spikes to snag Jin hulls.

sentences.zh: 先是，羊祜獲吳間諜，具知情狀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Hu had captured a Wu spy and learned the full situation.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu had already interrogated a Wu agent and knew every detail.

sentences.zh: 濬乃作大筏數十，亦方百餘步，縛草為人，被甲持杖，令善水者以筏先行，筏遇鐵錐，錐輒著筏去。

translations.literal: Jun then built several score great rafts, likewise over a hundred paces square, bound straw men armored and armed, ordered strong swimmers to pilot the rafts first; when a raft struck a spike the spike tore away with the raft.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun floated armored straw figures on massive rafts so the hidden spikes tore free when they struck.

sentences.zh: 又作火炬，長十餘丈，大數十圍，灌以麻油，在船前，遇鎖，然炬燒之，須臾，融液斷絕，於是船無所礙。

translations.literal: He also made torches tens of zhang long and tens of arm-spans thick, filled with sesame oil, set before the ships; when they met chains he lit the torches and in moments the metal melted and parted, so the ships met no obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Giant oiled torches melted the chains until the fleet could pass unhindered.

sentences.zh: 二月庚申，克吳西陵，獲其鎮南將軍留憲、征南將軍成據、宜都太守虞忠。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the second month he took Wu's Xiling, capturing garrison general Liu Xian, southern expedition general Cheng Ju, and Yidu governor Yu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-spring he stormed Xiling and seized Liu Xian, Cheng Ju, and Yidu's governor Yu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，克荊門、夷道二城，獲監軍陸晏。

translations.literal: On renxu he took the twin towns of Jingmen and Yidao, capturing overseer Lu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Jingmen and Yidao fell, along with the Wu overseer Lu Yan.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，克樂鄉，獲水軍督陸景。

translations.literal: On yichou he took Lexiang, capturing naval commander Lu Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Lexiang and captured the Wu fleet commander Lu Jing.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍施洪等來降。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Shi Hong and others came over.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong, general who pacifies the west, defected with his command.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔進濬為平東將軍、假節、都督益梁諸軍事。

translations.literal: On yihai an edict advanced Jun to general who pacifies the east, credential staff, and area commander for Yi and Liang forces.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him general who pacifies the east with acting credentials over Yi and Liang.

sentences.zh: 濬自發蜀，兵不血刃，攻無堅城，夏口、武昌，無相支抗。

translations.literal: From the day Jun left Shu his soldiers drew no blood yet took every walled town; Xiakou and Wuchang offered no resistance.
translations.idiomatic: His march downriver was a cascade of bloodless surrenders past Xiakou and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 於是順流鼓棹，徑造三山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rode the current, drums beating and oars pulling, and made straight for Three Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He then swept downstream toward Three Mountains.

sentences.zh: 皓遣遊擊將軍張象率舟軍萬人禦濬，象軍望旗而降。

translations.literal: Hao dispatched mobile corps general Zhang Xiang with a fleet of ten thousand to oppose Jun; Xiang's troops lowered their banners at sight of Jun's flags.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao sent Zhang Xiang with ten thousand sailors; they surrendered at the first glimpse of Wang Jun's standards.

sentences.zh: 皓聞濬軍旌旗器甲，屬天滿江，威勢甚盛，莫不破膽。

translations.literal: When Hao heard that Jun's banners and armor filled the sky and river, the majesty was so great that none did not lose courage.
translations.idiomatic: Word that Wang Jun's pennants blacked out the river broke Sun Hao's court.

sentences.zh: 用光祿薛瑩、中書令胡沖計，送降文於濬曰：「吳郡孫皓叩頭死罪。

translations.literal: Following the counsel of imperial household officer Xue Ying and palace secretary Hu Chong, he delivered a surrender text to Jun saying: "Sun Hao of Wu kowtows in mortal guilt.
translations.idiomatic: On Xue Ying's advice he sent a capitulation opening with "Sun Hao of Wu kowtows in guilt."

sentences.zh: 昔漢室失禦，九州幅裂，先人因時略有江南，遂阻山河，與魏乖隔。

translations.literal: Formerly the Han house lost the reins and the nine provinces split; our forebears seized the moment to hold the south of the Yangzi, then relied on mountains and rivers and stood apart from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled how Wu's founders carved out the south when the Han collapsed.

sentences.zh: 大晉龍興，德覆四海，暗劣偷安，未喻天命。

translations.literal: Great Jin rose like a dragon and its virtue roofs the four seas; we, dim and mean, clung to peace and did not grasp heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He admitted that Jin's virtue covered the realm while Wu clung to false security.

sentences.zh: 至於今者，猥煩六軍，衡蓋露次，還臨江渚。

translations.literal: As for now, we have presumptuously troubled the six armies; your canopies stand exposed along the shore as you return to the river islets.
translations.idiomatic: He described Jin's hosts camped along the shore as an unbearable humiliation.

sentences.zh: 舉國震惶，假息漏刻，敢緣天朝，含弘光大。

translations.literal: The whole state trembles, borrowing breath moment by moment; we dare rely on the celestial court's vast mercy.
translations.idiomatic: He begged for the conquerors' mercy.

sentences.zh: 謹遣私署太常張夔等奉所佩璽綬，委質請命。

translations.literal: We respectfully dispatch our privately appointed minister of rituals Zhang Kui and others bearing the seals and cords we wore, to submit our persons and beg for orders.
translations.idiomatic: He offered the imperial seals through an envoy named Zhang Kui.

sentences.zh: 」壬寅，濬入於石頭。

translations.literal: End-quote; on renyin Jun entered Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: On that day Wang Jun entered Shitou fortress.

sentences.zh: 皓乃備亡國之禮，素車白馬，肉袒面縛，銜璧牽羊，大夫衰服，士輿櫬，率其偽太子瑾、瑾弟魯王虔等二十一人，造於壘門。

translations.literal: Hao then prepared the rites of a conquered state—unpainted cart, white horse, bare chest with bound hands, jade disc in mouth and sheep led on a leash, great officers in mourning dress, gentlemen bearing a coffin—leading his false heir Jin, Jin's younger brother Prince of Lu Qian, and twenty others to the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao came in the full costume of submission—white cart, bound hands, jade in his mouth, sheep in tow, ministers mourning, a bier carried before him—leading the heir and princes to Wang Jun's camp.

sentences.zh: 濬躬解其縛，受璧焚櫬，送于京師。

translations.literal: Jun personally loosed his bonds, accepted the disc, burned the bier, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun cut his bonds, took the offering disc, burned the ritual bier, and sent him north to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 收其圖籍，封其府庫，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: He collected maps and registers, sealed storehouses, and the army took no private plunder.
translations.idiomatic: He secured archives and treasuries and kept the troops from looting.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者犒濬軍。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys to reward Jun's army.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent officers to feast his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 初，詔書使濬下建平，受杜預節度，至秣陵，受王渾節度。

translations.literal: Initially the edict ordered Jun downstream to Jianping under Du Yu's direction, and upon reaching Moling to obey Wang Hun's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier orders had placed him under Du Yu until Jianping and under Wang Hun at Moling.

sentences.zh: 預至江陵，謂諸將帥曰：「若濬得下建平，則順流長驅，威名已著，不宜令受制於我。

translations.literal: When Yu reached Jiangling he told the generals: "If Jun can take Jianping he will sweep downstream and his fame will be set; he should not be made subordinate to me.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu told his officers that if Wang Jun cleared Jianping he should not be tethered to his own command.

sentences.zh: 若不能克，則無緣得施節度。

translations.literal: If he cannot overcome it, then there is no occasion to exercise direction over him."
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Jun stalled, coordination would be pointless anyway.

sentences.zh: 」濬至西陵，預與之書曰：'足下既摧其西籓，便當徑取秣陵，討累世之逋寇，釋吳人於塗炭。

translations.literal: When Jun reached Xiling, Yu wrote him a letter saying: 'You have already broken their western shield; you ought to strike Moling directly, settle generations of fugitive rebels, and free Wu's people from fire and flood.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu urged him by letter to drive straight on Moling and finish the war.

sentences.zh: 自江入淮，逾於泗汴，溯河而上，振旅還都，亦曠世一事也。

translations.literal: From the Yangzi into the Huai, across the Si and Bian, up the Yellow River, then disband the host at the capital—such a deed would be unmatched in an age.'
translations.idiomatic: A victory march to Luoyang, he said, would crown the age.

sentences.zh: 」濬大悅，表呈預書。

translations.literal: End-quote; Jun was greatly pleased and forwarded Yu's letter in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Wang Jun submitted Du Yu's letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及濬將至秣陵，王渾遣信要令暫過論事，濬舉帆直指，報曰：「風利，不得泊也。

translations.literal: As Jun neared Moling, Wang Hun sent a messenger asking him to stop briefly to confer; Jun raised sail and pointed straight ahead, replying: "The wind favors me; I cannot anchor."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun demanded a parley; Wang Jun answered that a fair wind forbade stopping.

sentences.zh: 」王渾久破皓中軍，斬張悌等，頓兵不敢進。

translations.literal: End-quote; Wang Hun long ago had broken Hao's central army and beheaded Zhang Ti, yet halted his troops and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun had shattered Sun Hao's main force and killed Zhang Ti but then froze.

sentences.zh: 而濬乘勝納降，渾恥而且忿，乃表濬違詔不受節度，誣罪狀之。

translations.literal: Yet Jun rode victory to accept the surrender; Hun felt shame and anger, then memorialized that Jun disobeyed the edict and refused direction, framing crimes against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun took the credit for accepting surrender, so Wang Hun accused him of insubordination.

sentences.zh: 有司遂按濬檻車征，帝弗許，詔讓濬曰：「伐國事重，宜令有一。

translations.literal: The ministry then pressed to summon Jun in a caged cart; the emperor refused, issuing a reproof: "Attacking a state is weighty; command should be unified.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry wanted Wang Jun arrested; the emperor demurred but scolded him for divided command.

sentences.zh: 前詔使將軍受安車將軍渾節度，渾思謀深重，案甲以待將軍。

translations.literal: The prior edict ordered the general to accept direction from peace-chariot general Hun; Hun's plans run deep; he rested his armor awaiting the general.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had told Wang Jun to obey Wang Hun, who had halted deliberately for coordination.

sentences.zh: 云何徑前，不從渾命，違制昧利，甚失大義。

translations.literal: How could you press forward and ignore Hun's orders, violating regulation for gain—greatly losing in righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged him with rushing ahead for glory at the cost of good order.

sentences.zh: 將軍功勳，簡在朕心，當率由詔書，崇成王法，而於事終恃功肆意，朕將何以令天下？

translations.literal: The general's merit is recorded in Our heart; he should follow the edict and uphold the kingly law, yet in the end he relied on merit and acted as he pleased—how shall We command the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: He acknowledged Wang Jun's feat yet insisted that defying orders undermined the law.

sentences.zh: 」濬上書自理曰：

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial in his own defense, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun answered with a long self-defense.

sentences.zh: 渾又騰周浚書，雲濬軍得吳寶物。

translations.literal: Hun also forwarded Zhou Jun's letter alleging Jun's army had seized Wu treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun circulated Zhou Jun's claim that Wang Jun's men looted Wu's hoard.

sentences.zh: 濬復表曰：

translations.literal: Jun submitted another memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun filed a second rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 濬至京都，有司奏，濬表既不列前後所被七詔月日，又赦後違詔不受渾節度，大不敬，付廷尉科罪。

translations.literal: When Jun reached the capital the ministry reported that his memorial failed to list the dates of seven successive edicts and that after the amnesty he still disobeyed the edict and rejected Hun's direction—grave irreverence—and should be handed to the minister of justice for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang prosecutors wanted him tried for omitting edict dates and ignoring Wang Hun after the general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「濬前受詔徑造秣陵，後乃下受渾節度。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Jun first received an edict to go straight to Moling, and only afterward was he to obey Hun's direction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that Wang Jun had first been told to rush Moling, then to defer to Wang Hun.

sentences.zh: 詔書稽留，所下不至，便令與不受詔同責，未為經通。

translations.literal: Because the edicts were delayed in transmission, holding him as if he had never received them is not reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Late orders could not fairly be treated as refusal.

sentences.zh: 濬不即表上被渾宣詔，此可責也。

translations.literal: That Jun did not immediately memorialize when Hun proclaimed the edict may be blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Only the delay in reporting Wang Hun's message was culpable.

sentences.zh: 濬有征伐之勞，不足以一眚掩之。

translations.literal: Jun has merit in the campaign; it is not enough to bury that under a single fault."
translations.idiomatic: His conquest outweighed a minor slip.

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏，濬赦後燒賊船百三十五艘，輒敕付廷尉禁推。

translations.literal: The ministry again reported that after the amnesty Jun burned 135 enemy ships and should be remanded to the minister of justice for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Prosecutors also attacked him for burning 135 Wu ships after the pardon.

sentences.zh: 詔曰「勿推」。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Do not investigate."
translations.idiomatic: The throne told them to drop it.

sentences.zh: 拜濬輔國大將軍，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Jun was appointed bulwark-of-the-state grand general and colonel of infantry.
translations.idiomatic: He was named bulwark grand general and colonel of infantry.

sentences.zh: 舊校唯五，置此營自濬始也。

translations.literal: Formerly there were only five colonels; establishing this camp began with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth infantry colonelcy was created for him.

sentences.zh: 有司又奏，輔國依比，未為達官，不置司馬，不給官騎。

translations.literal: The ministry again argued that, by precedent, bulwark grand general was not a top post, so it should have no major, no official mounts.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks claimed the new title lacked senior perquisites.

sentences.zh: 詔依征鎮給五百大車，增兵五百人為輔國營，給親騎百人、官騎十人，置司馬。

translations.literal: An edict granted him five hundred supply wagons as for a field commander, added five hundred soldiers to his bulwark camp, gave him a hundred personal riders and ten official mounts, and assigned a major.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor overruled them with wagons, escort, and a staff major.

sentences.zh: 封為襄陽縣侯，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed marquis of Xiangyang county with ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He received a marquisate of Xiangyang with a ten-thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 封子彝楊鄉亭侯，邑千五百戶，賜絹萬匹，又賜衣一襲、錢三十萬及食物。

translations.literal: His son Yi was made village marquis of Yang township with fifteen hundred households; he was given ten thousand bolts of silk, one full set of robes, three hundred thousand cash, and foodstuffs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi gained a lesser marquisate, silk, robes, cash, and provisions.

sentences.zh: 濬自以功大，而為渾父子及豪強所抑，屢為有司所奏，每進見，陳其攻伐之勞，及見枉之狀，或不勝忿憤，徑出不辭。

translations.literal: Jun deemed his achievement great yet was checked by Hun and his son and by powerful families; repeatedly the ministry indicted him; each time he entered audience he stated his campaign's toil and how he had been wronged, sometimes unable to contain rage and leaving without leave.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his reward meager, he quarreled with Wang Hun's faction, railed at audiences, and stormed out.

sentences.zh: 帝每容恕之。

translations.literal: The emperor always indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu bore with his outbursts.

sentences.zh: 益州護軍範通，濬之外親也。

translations.literal: Fan Tong, protector of armies in Yi, was Jun's relative by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His in-law Fan Tong, protector in Yi, offered counsel.

sentences.zh: 謂濬曰：「卿功則美矣，然恨所以居美者，未盡善也。

translations.literal: He told Jun: "Your deed is splendid, yet I regret that how you wear the splendor is not the best."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tong said his victory was glorious but his conduct afterward was not.

sentences.zh: 」濬曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: End-quote; Jun said: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun asked what he meant.

sentences.zh: 」通曰：「卿旋旆之日，角巾私第，口不言平吳之事。

translations.literal: End-quote; Tong said: "On the day you lowered the banners you should have worn a scholar's kerchief in your private home and never spoken of pacifying Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tong advised him to have gone home modestly and stayed silent about the conquest.

sentences.zh: 若有問者，輒曰：'聖主之德，群帥之力，老夫何力之有焉！

translations.literal: If anyone asked, you should always answer: 'The sage ruler's virtue and the host of commanders' strength—what did this old man do?'
translations.idiomatic: He should have credited only the emperor and his comrades.

sentences.zh: '如斯，顏老之不伐，龔遂之雅對，將何以過之。

translations.literal: Had you done so, the old Yan Hui's refusal to boast or Gong Sui's tactful replies could not surpass you.
translations.idiomatic: Such humility would have rivaled ancient paragons.

sentences.zh: 藺生所以屈廉頗，王渾能無愧乎！

translations.literal: This is how Lin Xiangru humbled Lian Po—could Wang Hun feel shame?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tong hinted that humility would have shamed Wang Hun as Lian Po was shamed.

sentences.zh: 」濬曰：「吾始懼鄧艾之事，畏禍及，不得無言，亦不能遣諸胸中，是吾偏也。

translations.literal: End-quote; Jun said: "At first I feared Deng Ai's fate and dared not stay silent; I could not drive it from my breast—this is my bias."
