translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun answered that fear of another Deng Ai trap had forced him to speak his mind.

sentences.zh: 」時人咸以濬功重報輕，博士秦秀、太子洗馬孟康、前溫令李密等並表訟濬之屈。

translations.literal: People of the time all thought Jun's merit heavy and his reward light; academicians Qin Xiu, crown prince attendant Meng Kang, former magistrate of Wen Li Mi, and others jointly memorialized to redress Jun's wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars petitioned, saying his honors were unjustly slight.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遷濬鎮軍大將軍，加散騎常侍，領後軍將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor then promoted Jun to garrison grand general, added regular attendant-in-ordinary, and concurrent general of the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: The court raised him to garrison grand general with a rear-army command.

sentences.zh: 王渾詣濬，濬嚴設備衛，然後見之，其相猜防如此。

translations.literal: When Wang Hun called on Jun, Jun arrayed guards before receiving him; such was their mutual suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun had to pass a cordon of guards to see him.

sentences.zh: 濬平吳之後，以勳高位重，不復素業自居，乃玉食錦服，縱奢侈以自逸。

translations.literal: After pacifying Wu, Jun, because of high merit and rank, no longer lived as in his plain days; he ate from jade vessels and dressed in brocade, indulging extravagance to please himself.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest he flaunted wealth—jade tableware, brocade robes, lavish ease.

sentences.zh: 其有辟引，多是蜀人，示不遺故舊也。

translations.literal: When he recruited followers they were mostly Shu men, showing he did not forget old associates.
translations.idiomatic: He favored Shu-born aides to remember old ties.

sentences.zh: 後又轉濬撫軍大將軍、開府儀同三司，加特進，散騎常侍、後軍將軍如故。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to bulwark grand general, granted independent headquarters with rites matching the Three Excellencies, added the eminent prestige title tejin, keeping regular attendant and general of the rear army as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made bulwark grand general with separate headquarters equaling the Three Excellencies, honored with the tejin distinction, and kept his old concurrent posts.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年八十，諡曰武。

translations.literal: He died at eighty; his posthumous name was Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty with the posthumous epithet Wu, "martial."

sentences.zh: 葬柏谷山，大營塋域，葬垣周四十五里，面別開一門，松柏茂盛。

translations.literal: He was buried on Mount Baigu with a vast necropolis: the burial wall ran forty-five li around with a separate gate on each face and luxuriant pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: His tomb on Mount Baigu sprawled over forty-five li of walled parkland.

sentences.zh: 子矩嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ju succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Ju inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 矩弟暢，散騎郎。

translations.literal: Ju's younger brother Chang was a gentleman cavalry attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju's brother Wang Chang served as gentleman cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 暢子粹，，武帝詔粹尚潁川公主，仕至魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Chang's son Cui—an edict of Emperor Wu ordered Cui to marry the Princess of Yingchuan; he rose to governor of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang's son Wang Cui married the Princess of Yingchuan and became governor of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 濬有二孫，過江不見齒錄。

translations.literal: Jun had two grandsons who crossed the southward exodus but were omitted from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Two grandsons fled south with the court yet went unrecorded in the rolls.

sentences.zh: 安西將軍恆溫鎮江陵，表言之曰：「臣聞崇德賞功，為政之所先；

translations.literal: General Who Guards the West Huan Wen garrisoned Jiangling and memorialized, saying: "Your servant has heard that honoring virtue and rewarding merit comes first in government;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, guarding Jiangling, argued that rewards should favor old service.

sentences.zh: 興滅繼絕，百王之所務。

translations.literal: restoring fallen lines is the business of every king."
translations.idiomatic: He cited the duty to preserve extinguished houses.

sentences.zh: 故德參時雍，則奕世承祀；

translations.literal: Thus when virtue joins the harmonious age, offerings continue for generations;
translations.idiomatic: Merit and virtue, he said, deserved perpetual remembrance.

sentences.zh: 功烈一代，則永錫祚胤。

translations.literal: when achievement shines for a generation, blessings should extend to descendants forever."
translations.idiomatic: He tied honors for heirs to dynastic gratitude.

sentences.zh: 案故撫軍王濬曆職內外，任兼文武，料敵制勝，明勇獨斷，義存社稷之利，不顧專輒之罪。

translations.literal: The late bulwark grand general Wang Jun served inside and outside, held civil and military posts together, sized foes and seized victory, showed insight and courage and decided alone, upholding the altars' good without regard for acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Wang Jun's lone decision to save the realm.

sentences.zh: 荷戈長鶩，席捲萬里，僭號之吳，面縛象魏，今皇澤被于九州，玄風洽于區外，襄陽之封，廢而莫續；

translations.literal: Bearing halberds he swept ten thousand li; the usurping state of Wu bound itself at the royal court; now imperial grace spreads through the nine provinces and subtle teaching reaches beyond the borders, yet the Xiangyang enfeoffment lies abolished without continuation;
translations.idiomatic: He noted that Jin ruled all under heaven while Wang Jun's marquisate lapsed.

sentences.zh: 恩寵之號，墜於近嗣。

translations.literal: favors and noble titles have fallen away from the near descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor had not reached the living line.

sentences.zh: 遐邇酸懷，臣竊悼之。

translations.literal: Near and far are heartsore; your servant privately grieves.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen said the neglect shamed the court.

sentences.zh: 濬今有二孫，年出六十，室如懸磬，糊口江濱，四節蒸嘗，菜羹不給。

translations.literal: Jun now has two grandsons past sixty; their houses are empty as hanging harps; they scrape a living along the river and cannot supply even vegetable soup for the seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Two grandsons lived in destitution by the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高定業，求樂毅之嗣；

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu settled the realm he sought the heirs of Yue Yi;
translations.idiomatic: He compared them to Gaozu's care for Yue Yi's line.

sentences.zh: 世祖旌賢，建葛亮之胤。

translations.literal: when Guangwu honored the worthy he established Zhuge Liang's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: And to Guangwu's revival of Zhuge Liang's house.

sentences.zh: 夫效忠異代，立功異國，尚通天下之善，使不泯棄，況濬建元勳于當年，著喜慶於身後，靈基托根于南垂，皇祚中興于江左，舊物克彰，神器重耀，豈不由伊人之功力也哉！

translations.literal: Those who gave loyalty in another age and merit in another state still received the world's good offices so they would not vanish—how much more Jun, who founded the founding achievement in his own day and left auspicious signs after death, whose spirit line took root on the southern edge while the imperial house revived on the left bank of the Yangzi; old tokens were restored and the sacred vessel shone again—was it not through such men's strength?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's foundational merit for the eastern Jin restoration deserved the same care.

sentences.zh: 誠宜加恩，少垂矜憫，追錄舊勳，纂錫茅土。

translations.literal: Truly it is fitting to add favor, show a little pity, trace the old merit, and renew the fief of reed-sprig.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that their fief be restored.

sentences.zh: 則聖朝之恩，宣暢于上，忠臣之志，不墜於地矣。

translations.literal: Then the sage court's grace will shine above and loyal ministers' intent will not fall to earth."
translations.idiomatic: Only then would grace and loyalty align.

sentences.zh: 」卒不見省。

translations.literal: End-quote; in the end it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court never acted on the plea.

sentences.zh: 唐彬

translations.literal: Tang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin

sentences.zh: 唐彬，字儒宗，魯國鄒人也。

translations.literal: Tang Bin, courtesy name Ruzong, was a man of Zou in the state of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin, courtesy name Ruzong, came from Zou in Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父台，太山太守。

translations.literal: His father Tai was governor of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tang Tai had been governor of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 彬有經國大度，而不拘行檢。

translations.literal: Bin had the breadth to order the state yet did not fuss over personal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin thought like a statesman and cared little for petty respectability.

sentences.zh: 少便弓馬，好遊獵，身長八尺，走及奔鹿，強力兼人。

translations.literal: From youth he was skilled at bow and horse, loved roaming and hunting, stood eight chi tall, could run with a fleeing deer, and his strength surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a superb rider and archer, stood eight feet tall, could outrun a deer, and out-muscled ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 晚乃敦悅經史，尤明《易經》，隨師受業，還家教授，恆數百人。

translations.literal: Only later did he earnestly delight in the classics and histories, especially mastering the "Book of Changes"; he studied with teachers, then returned home to teach, always several hundred pupils.
translations.idiomatic: Later he immersed himself in the canon, above all the "Changes," studied abroad, and came home to lecture to hundreds.

sentences.zh: 初為郡門下掾，轉主簿。

translations.literal: He first served as clerk at the commandery gate, then transferred to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a commandery gate clerk and rose to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 刺史王沈集諸參佐，盛論距吳之策，以問九郡吏。

translations.literal: Inspector Wang Shen assembled his staff to debate strategies for resisting Wu and polled the clerks of nine commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wang Shen convened his aides to plan anti-Wu strategy and canvassed clerks from nine jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 彬與譙郡主張惲俱陳吳有可兼之勢，沈善其對。

translations.literal: Bin and Zhang Yun, chief of Qiao commandery, both argued Wu could be overrun; Shen praised their answers.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin and Zhang Yun of Qiao argued that Wu could be taken; Wang Shen approved.

sentences.zh: 又使彬難言吳未可伐者，而辭理皆屈。

translations.literal: Shen also had Bin refute those who said Wu could not be attacked, and their rhetoric and logic all bent.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Tang Bin dismantle the anti-war case until every objection collapsed.

sentences.zh: 還遷功曹，舉孝廉，州辟主簿，累遷別駕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to merit assessor, recommended as filial and incorrupt, summoned as chief clerk by the province, and rose in stages to chief clerk on the inspector's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced through merit assessor, filial-and-incorrupt nomination, and provincial chief clerk to senior adjutant.

sentences.zh: 彬忠肅公亮，盡規匡救，不顯諫以自彰，又奉使詣相府計事，于時僚佐皆當世英彥，見彬莫不欽悅，稱之于文帝，薦為掾屬。

translations.literal: Bin was loyal, solemn, fair, and bright; he offered full remonstrance and rescue without flashy admonition to glorify himself. Sent on mission to the minister's bureau, the staff there were the age's finest talents; seeing Bin they all admired him, praised him to Prince Wen, and recommended him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and blunt in counsel, he served the chancellery mission so well that Sima Zhao's brilliant staff praised him to Prince Wen.

sentences.zh: 帝以問其參軍孔顥，顥忌其能，良久不答。

translations.literal: The prince asked his adjutant Kong Hao, who envied Bin's ability and for a long time did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao asked Kong Hao, who stayed silent out of jealousy.

sentences.zh: 陳騫在坐，斂板而稱曰：「彬之為人，勝騫甚遠。

translations.literal: Chen Qian was present, folded his tablet and declared: "As a man, Bin surpasses Qian by far."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian broke in: "Tang Bin is far my superior."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「但能如卿，固未易得，何論於勝。

translations.literal: End-quote; the prince laughed and said: "Merely to match you is already hard to obtain; how speak of surpassing?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao laughed that matching Chen Qian was rare enough, let alone surpassing him.

sentences.zh: 」因辟彬為鎧曹屬。

translations.literal: End-quote; therefore he summoned Bin to the armory bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He hired Tang Bin for the armory office.

sentences.zh: 帝問曰：「卿何以致辟？

translations.literal: The prince asked: "How did you earn the summons?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao asked how he had won the post.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「修業陋巷，觀古人之遺跡，言滿天下無口過，行滿天下無怨惡。

translations.literal: End-quote; he replied: "I cultivated learning in a humble lane, observed the traces of the ancients, spoke under heaven without slip of the tongue, acted under heaven without incurring hatred."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin cited modest study, imitation of antiquity, and blameless speech and conduct.

sentences.zh: 」帝顧四坐曰：「名不虛行。

translations.literal: End-quote; the prince looked around the hall and said: "The name was not empty."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao told the room the reputation was deserved.

sentences.zh: 」他日，謂孔顥曰：「近見唐彬，卿受蔽賢之責矣。」

translations.literal: Another day he told Kong Hao: "I have lately seen Tang Bin; you bear the blame for hiding talent."
translations.idiomatic: Later he rebuked Kong Hao for concealing Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 初，鄧艾之誅也，文帝以艾久在隴右，素得士心，一旦夷滅，恐邊情搔動，使彬密察之。

translations.literal: When Deng Ai was executed, Prince Wen, because Ai had long been on the Longyou frontier and won soldiers' hearts, feared border unrest if he were suddenly wiped out, and sent Bin to spy.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing mutiny after Deng Ai's death, Sima Zhao sent Tang Bin to sound Longyou opinion.

sentences.zh: 彬還，白帝曰：「鄧艾忌克詭狹，矜能負才，順從者謂為見事，直言者謂之觸迕。

translations.literal: Bin returned and reported: "Deng Ai was jealous, harsh, and narrow, prided himself on ability and talent; those who flattered him he deemed insightful, those who spoke straight he deemed offensive."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin reported that Deng Ai had been jealous and petty, punishing candor and rewarding flattery.

sentences.zh: 雖長史司馬，參佐牙門，答對失指，輒見罵辱。

translations.literal: Even senior scribes, majors, staff, and gate officers who answered slightly wrong were reviled and insulted.
translations.idiomatic: Even senior aides who misspoke faced abuse.

sentences.zh: 處身無禮，大失人心。

translations.literal: He conducted himself without ritual and greatly lost men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: His rudeness had cost him every bond of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 又好施行事役，數勞眾力。

translations.literal: He also loved launching labor projects and repeatedly exhausted the masses.
translations.idiomatic: He had also worn the people out with endless corvée.

sentences.zh: 隴右甚患苦之，喜聞其禍，不肯為用。

translations.literal: Longyou bitterly suffered and rejoiced at his fall; they were unwilling to be used for him.
translations.idiomatic: The northwesterners hated him and would not rally to his memory.

sentences.zh: 今諸軍已至，足以鎮壓內外，願無以為慮。」

translations.literal: Now the host has arrived and can pacify inside and outside; I pray Your Highness not to worry." End-quote.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's army could hold the region; Tang Bin urged Sima Zhao not to fret.

sentences.zh: 俄除尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed gentleman of the Ministry of Works water section.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named waterworks secretary in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was granted a marquisate within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he received a marquisate within the passes.

sentences.zh: 出補鄴令，彬道德齊禮，期月化成。

translations.literal: Posted as magistrate of Ye, Bin guided the people with virtue and rites; in one cycle customs were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Ye he ruled through ritual and remade local custom in a month.

sentences.zh: 遷弋陽太守，明設禁防，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Promoted to governor of Yiyang, he set clear prohibitions and defenses; the hundred surnames were secure.
translations.idiomatic: As Yiyang's governor he posted clear laws and kept the people safe.

sentences.zh: 以母喪去官。

translations.literal: He left office for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 益州東接吳寇，監軍位缺，朝議用武陵太守楊宗及彬。

translations.literal: Yi Province bordered Wu raiders; the overseer post was vacant, and court debate named Wuling governor Yang Zong and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: With Yi Province facing Wu and the overseer seat empty, the court shortlisted Yang Zong and Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 武帝以問散騎常侍文立，立曰：「宗、彬俱不可失。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu asked regular attendant Wen Li, who said: "Neither Zong nor Bin can be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu polled Wen Li, who refused to choose between them.

sentences.zh: 然彬多財欲，而宗好酒，惟陛下裁之。

translations.literal: Yet Bin is driven by greed for wealth, while Zong loves wine—only Your Majesty may decide."
translations.idiomatic: He warned that Tang Bin loved money and Yang Zong loved drink.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「財欲可足，酒者難改。

translations.literal: End-quote; the emperor said: "Greed for wealth can be satisfied; drink is hard to change."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged greed easier to curb than alcoholism.

sentences.zh: 」遂用彬。

translations.literal: End-quote; Bin was therefore chosen.
translations.idiomatic: He picked Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔彬監巴東諸軍事，加廣武將軍。

translations.literal: Soon another edict ordered Bin to oversee Ba-East military affairs and added the title Guangwu general.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin was soon made overseer of Ba-East with the rank of Guangwu general.

sentences.zh: 上征吳之策，甚合帝意。

translations.literal: He presented a plan to attack Wu that matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: His Wu campaign memorial suited Emperor Wu perfectly.

sentences.zh: 後與王濬共伐吳，彬屯據沖要，為眾軍前驅。

translations.literal: Later, campaigning with Wang Jun, he held the choke points and spearheaded the host.
translations.idiomatic: Beside Wang Jun he seized critical ground and led the van.

sentences.zh: 每設疑兵，應機制勝，陷西陵、樂鄉，多所擒獲。

translations.literal: Whenever he deployed decoys he seized victory as chance allowed, took Xiling and Lexiang, and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: Feints and timing won Xiling and Lexiang with heavy captures.

sentences.zh: 自巴陵、沔口以東，諸賊所聚，莫不震懼，倒戈肉袒。

translations.literal: From Baling and Miankou eastward every bandit stronghold trembled, dropped weapons, and bared their chests in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: East of Baling and the Han estuary every Wu garrison panicked and capitulated.

sentences.zh: 彬知賊寇已殄，孫皓將降，未至建鄴二百里，稱疾遲留，以示不競。

translations.literal: Bin knew the bandits were finished and Sun Hao would submit; two hundred li short of Jianye he claimed illness and lingered to show he would not compete.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing victory certain, he halted two hundred li from Jianye feigning illness so no one could accuse him of racing for glory.

sentences.zh: 果有先到者爭物，後到者爭功，于時有識莫不高彬此舉。

translations.literal: Sure enough the first arrivals squabbled over plunder and the latecomers over credit; thoughtful men all esteemed Bin for this act.
translations.idiomatic: While early victors fought over loot and credit, observers praised his restraint.

sentences.zh: 吳平，詔曰：「廣武將軍唐彬受任方隅，東禦吳寇，南監蠻越，撫寧疆埸，有綏禦之績。

translations.literal: When Wu fell an edict said: "Guangwu general Tang Bin, charged with a corner of the realm, guarded east against Wu and south against Man and Yue, quieted the frontier, and kept peace with soothing authority.
translations.idiomatic: The victory edict praised Tang Bin for holding the southeast and pacifying barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又每慷慨，志在立功。

translations.literal: Moreover he was always fervent, his intent set on merit.
translations.idiomatic: It noted his zeal for service.

sentences.zh: 頃者征討，扶疾奉命，首啟戎行，獻俘授馘，勳效顯著。

translations.literal: Lately in the campaign he accepted orders though ill, opened the march, presented captives and severed ears, and his achievement shone.
translations.idiomatic: Despite illness he had led the van and delivered captives.

sentences.zh: 其以彬為右將軍、都督巴東諸軍事。

translations.literal: Therefore appoint Bin general of the right and area commander of Ba-East military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: He was named general of the right with Ba-East command.

sentences.zh: 」徵拜翊軍校尉，改封上庸縣侯，食邑六千戶，賜絹六千匹。

translations.literal: End-quote; summoned as colonel of the guards of the wings, re-enfeoffed marquis of Shangyong county with six thousand households, given six thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as colonel of the wing guards, he gained a Shangyong marquisate, six thousand households, and silk.

sentences.zh: 朝有疑議，每參預焉。

translations.literal: Whenever court debate stalled he took part.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in on doubtful policy debates.

sentences.zh: 北虜侵掠北平，以彬為使持節、監幽州諸軍事、領護烏丸校尉、右將軍。

translations.literal: Northern tribes raided Beiping; Bin was made credential bearer, overseer of You Province military affairs, concurrent protector-colonel of the Wuhuan, and general of the right.
translations.idiomatic: When steppe raiders hit Beiping, he became Youzhou overseer, Wuhuan protector-colonel, and general of the right.

sentences.zh: 彬既至鎮，訓卒利兵，廣農重稼，震威耀武，宣喻國命，示以恩信。

translations.literal: Once at his post he drilled troops and sharpened weapons, expanded farming and valued grain, displayed might, proclaimed the state's commands, and showed grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He trained soldiers, pushed agriculture, flashed force, and broadcast Jin's good faith.

sentences.zh: 於是鮮卑二部大莫廆、擿何等並遣侍子入貢。

translations.literal: Thereupon the two Xianbei divisions under Damokuai, Zhihe, and others each sent hostages and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Two Xianbei confederations under Damokuai and Zhihe sent hostages and gifts.

sentences.zh: 兼修學校，誨誘無倦，仁惠廣被。

translations.literal: He also restored schools, taught tirelessly, and spread benevolence broadly.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt schools and taught patiently until his kindness covered the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遂開拓舊境，卻地千里。

translations.literal: He therefore reopened old borders and pushed the frontier back a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered a thousand li of lost ground.

sentences.zh: 復秦長城塞，自溫城洎于碣石，綿亙山谷且三千里，分軍屯守，烽堠相望。

translations.literal: He repaired the Qin dynasty's long-wall line from Wencheng to Jieshi, spanning ravines and peaks for nearly three thousand li, posting garrisons so beacon towers sighted one another.
translations.idiomatic: He refortified the Qin wall from Wencheng to Jieshi, nearly three thousand li of watchtowers and camps.

sentences.zh: 由是邊境獲安，無犬吠之警，自漢魏征鎮莫之比焉。

translations.literal: Hence the border knew peace without dog-bark alarms; no Han or Wei frontier command could compare.
translations.idiomatic: The steppe fell so quiet that no Han or Wei frontier had matched it.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑諸種畏懼，遂殺大莫廆。

translations.literal: The Xianbei clans feared him and therefore killed Damokuai.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing him, the Xianbei assassinated Damokuai.

sentences.zh: 彬欲討之，恐列上俟報，虜必逃散，乃發幽冀車牛。

translations.literal: Bin wished to punish them but feared that memorializing and awaiting reply would let the raiders scatter, so he mobilized carts and oxen of You and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Planning a punitive strike without losing surprise, he requisitioned transport across You and Ji.

sentences.zh: 參軍許祗密奏之。

translations.literal: Staff officer Xu Zhi secretly memorialized against it.
translations.idiomatic: His adjutant Xu Zhi tattled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔遣御史檻車征彬付廷尉，以事直見釋。

translations.literal: An edict sent censors to haul Bin to the minister of justice in a cage cart, but he was released when the facts proved just.
translations.idiomatic: Censors jailed him until an inquiry cleared his action.

sentences.zh: 百姓追慕彬功德，生為立碑作頌。

translations.literal: The people mourned Bin's virtue and merit and erected a living stele with a hymn.
translations.idiomatic: Locals raised a stele praising him while he still lived.

sentences.zh: 彬初受學于東海閻德，門徒甚多，獨目彬有廊廟才。

translations.literal: Bin first studied under Yan De of Donghai, who had many disciples yet singled out Bin as having ministerial talent.
translations.idiomatic: His teacher Yan De of Donghai, amid hundreds of pupils, marked him for high office.

sentences.zh: 及彬官成，而德已卒，乃為之立碑。

translations.literal: When Bin's career matured, De had already died, so he raised a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Bin rose, Yan De was dead, so he honored him with a monument.

sentences.zh: 元康初，拜使持節、前將軍、領西戎校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang he was appointed credential bearer, forward general, concurrent colonel of the western tribes, and inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he became forward general, western-tribes colonel, and Yongzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 下教曰：「此州名都，士人林藪。

translations.literal: He issued an instruction saying: "This province is a famed metropolis and a forest of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed Yongzhou a haven of scholars.

sentences.zh: 處士皇甫申叔、嚴舒龍、姜茂時、梁子遠等，並志節清妙，履行高潔。

translations.literal: Recluses Huangfu Shenshu, Yan Shulong, Jiang Maoshi, Liang Ziyuan and others alike keep lofty resolve and pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He named recluses whose integrity shone.

sentences.zh: 踐境望風，虛心饑渴，思加延致，待以不臣之典。

translations.literal: Crossing the border I admire them on the wind; with humble mind and thirsty longing I wish to summon them with rites not binding a subject.
translations.idiomatic: He invited them with honors fit for peers, not underlings.

sentences.zh: 幅巾相見，論道而已，豈以吏職，屈染高規。

translations.literal: We shall meet in scholar's kerchiefs and discuss the Way alone—how could official duties stain high standards?
translations.idiomatic: He promised philosophical conversation without bureaucratic condescension.

sentences.zh: 郡國備禮發遣，以副於邑之望。

translations.literal: Let commanderies prepare full rites and send them forth to match the county's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered counties to escort them with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」於是四人皆到，彬敬而待之。

translations.literal: End-quote; thereupon all four arrived, and Bin received them with respect.
translations.idiomatic: All four came, and Tang Bin treated them deferentially.

sentences.zh: 卒官，時年六十，諡曰襄，賜絹二百匹，錢二十萬。

translations.literal: He died in office at sixty; his posthumous name was Xiang; he was given two hundred bolts of silk and two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He died on duty at sixty with the posthumous name Xiang, plus silk and cash.

sentences.zh: 長子嗣，官至廣陵太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Si reached the post of governor of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Tang Si became governor of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 少子岐，征虜司馬。

translations.literal: His younger son Qi was major on the staff of the general who conquers captives.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Tang Qi served as major to the general who conquers captives.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Shi ping.
translations.idiomatic: Historians' judgment

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孫氏負江山之阻隔，恃牛鬥之妖氛，奄有水鄉，抗衡上國。

translations.literal: The historiographers said: The Sun clan relied on river and mountain barriers and on the baleful vapors of the Dipper; they suddenly held the water country and stood against the superior state.
translations.idiomatic: The editors write that Sun Wu used terrain and astrology to defy the north.

sentences.zh: 二王屬當戎旅，受律遄征，渾既獻捷橫江，濬亦克清建鄴。

translations.literal: The two Wangs took up arms, received the baton and sped on campaign; Hun presented victory at Hengjiang and Jun likewise cleared Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Both Wangs campaigned: Wang Hun triumphed at Hengjiang and Wang Jun took Jianye.

sentences.zh: 于時討吳之役，將帥雖多，定吳之功，此焉為最。

translations.literal: In the Wu punitive expedition many were generals, yet for settling Wu this was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Many commanded, but they decided Wu's fate.

sentences.zh: 向使弘范父之不伐，慕陽夏之推功，上稟廟堂，下憑將士。

translations.literal: Had they broadened Fan Wuzi's refusal to boast and emulated the Yangxia habit of yielding credit—above obeying the court, below relying on the soldiery—
translations.idiomatic: Had they shown Fan Wenzi's modesty and Chen Shi's generosity, trusting throne and troops,

sentences.zh: 豈非茂勳茂德，善始善終者歟！

translations.literal: would they not have been splendid merit and splendid virtue, well begun and well ended!
translations.idiomatic: they might have matched the best beginnings and endings.

sentences.zh: 此而不存，彼焉是務。

translations.literal: Rejecting this yet chasing that—
translations.idiomatic: Ignoring that example while chasing lesser goals—

sentences.zh: 或矜功負氣，或恃勢驕陵，競構南箕，成茲貝錦。

translations.literal: some prided themselves on merit and nursed pride, some trusted power and bullied others, vying to frame rivals like the Southern Dipper, weaving slander like shell-patterned brocade.
translations.idiomatic: they flaunted pride, abused power, and traded accusations like court intriguers.

sentences.zh: 遂乃喧黷宸扆，斁亂彝倫，既為戒于功臣，亦致譏於清論，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: Thus they clamored before the throne, disrupted proper relations, became a warning to merit-holders, and earned censure from pure critics—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Their quarrels shamed the court and warned future generals—a pity.

sentences.zh: 王濟遂驕父之褊心，乖爭子之明義，俊材雖多，亦奚以為也。

translations.literal: Wang Ji then swelled with his father's narrow heart and betrayed a good son's duty; however talented, of what use?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji aped his father's pettiness and scanted filial duty despite his gifts.

sentences.zh: 唐彬畏避交爭，屬疾遲留，退讓之風，賢於渾濬遠矣。

translations.literal: Tang Bin shrank from rivalry, claimed illness and delayed—the temper of yielding was far worthier than Hun and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin's feigned delay showed a humility Wang Hun and Wang Jun lacked.

sentences.zh: 傳云「不拘行檢」，安得長者之行哉！

translations.literal: The tradition says he "did not fuss over conduct"—how can that be the walk of an elder?
translations.idiomatic: The text calls him lax in deportment, yet his choices were those of a true elder.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：二王總戎，淮海攸同。

translations.literal: Encomium: The two Wangs commanded arms; the Huai and sea shared the task.
translations.idiomatic: The ode praises both Wangs on the Huai front.

sentences.zh: 渾既害善，濬亦矜功。

translations.literal: Hun harmed the good; Jun prided himself on merit.
translations.idiomatic: One envied worthies; the other boasted.

sentences.zh: 武子豪桀，夙參朝列。

translations.literal: Wuzi the hero early joined the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, Wuzi, swaggered in office young.

sentences.zh: 逞欲牛心，紆情馬埒。

translations.literal: He indulged his whim for ox hearts and poured passion into the horse course.
translations.idiomatic: He wasted wit on wagers and racetracks.

sentences.zh: 儒宗知退，避名全節。

translations.literal: Ruzong knew retreat, shunned fame, and preserved integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin, Ruzong, chose retreat and kept his honor.
